Richmond upon Thames' population increased by around 8,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 200,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Richmond upon Thames increased by 4.4%, from just under 187,000 in 2011 to around 195,300 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of London (7.7%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Richmond upon Thames was home to around 24.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 23.3 in 2011. This area was among the top 20% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Richmond upon Thames than across London

An older Richmond upon Thames

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Richmond upon Thames increased by three years, from 38 to 41 years of age.

This area had the joint highest average (median) age in London (alongside Bromley) and a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just under 7,300 (an increase of 22.8%), while the number of residents between 25 and 34 years fell by just over 6,500 (22.8% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 3.0 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Changing relationships in Richmond upon Thames

Richmond upon Thames saw England's largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (from 36.7% in 2011 to 35.9% in 2021).

Hounslow saw the country's next largest decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (from 38.5% in 2011 to 38.3% in 2021).

Across London, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership increased from 44.1% to 46.2%, while the percentage in nearby Hounslow fell from 38.5% to 38.3%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Richmond upon Thames decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Family in Richmond upon Thames

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Richmond upon Thames, but fell across England.

In Richmond upon Thames, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 22.7% in 2011 to 24.9% in 2021, while across England it fell from 19.3% to 18.9%. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 17.8% to 18.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Richmond upon Thames fell from 18.6% to 16.9%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 4.7% to 5.7%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Richmond upon Thames increased by 2.2 percentage points

Employment in Richmond upon Thames

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell here, but rose across London.

In Richmond upon Thames, the percentage who were employed fell from 64.6% in 2011 to 61.4% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 58.6% to 59.4%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Richmond upon Thames increased from 2.8% to 3.0%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 16.6% to 18.1%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Richmond upon Thames decreased by 3.1 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

In 2021, 11.2% of Richmond upon Thames residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.1% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in Richmond upon Thames (2.1 percentage points) was similar to the increase across London (1.9 percentage points, from 8.8% to 10.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Richmond upon Thames increased by 2.1 percentage points

Richmond upon Thames residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 132,200 Richmond upon Thames residents said they were born in England. This represented 67.7% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 133,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 71.5% of Richmond upon Thames' population.

Non-EU European countries (other than the UK and Turkey) were the next most represented, with around 3,700 Richmond upon Thames residents reporting one of these countries as their country of birth (1.9%). This figure was up from around 2,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.2% of the population of Richmond upon Thames.

The number of Richmond upon Thames residents born in Scotland fell from just over 3,800 in 2011 (2.0% of the local population) to around 3,400 in 2021 (1.7%).

In 2021, 67.7% of Richmond upon Thames residents reported their country of birth as England

Ethnic groups in Richmond upon Thames

In 2021, 5.5% of Richmond upon Thames residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 3.6% in 2011. The 1.8 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across London, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 5.0% to 5.7%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 80.5% of people in Richmond upon Thames identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 86.0% in 2011), while 8.9% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 7.3% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.6% in 2011 to 3.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 5.5% of usual residents in Richmond upon Thames identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category

Disability in Richmond upon Thames

In 2021, 4.8% of Richmond upon Thames residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 12 people (8.1%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 7.9% in 2011. The proportion of Richmond upon Thames residents who were not disabled increased from 86.2% to 87.1%.

This area had Greater London's second lowest proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. Across the region, only City of London, with 3.9%, had a lower proportion.

Because of its small size, comparisons to City of London should be made with caution.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Richmond upon Thames decreased by 1.1 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in nearby Hounslow (7.5 percentage points) than in Richmond upon Thames (2.9 percentage points).

In Richmond upon Thames, the percentage of private renting increased from 21.8% in 2011 to 24.7% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Hounslow increased from 23.4% to 30.9%.

The rate of social renting in Richmond upon Thames fell from 12.6% to 12.1%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 63.6% to 62.4%.

Private renting in Richmond upon Thames increased by 2.9 percentage points

Health in Richmond upon Thames

In 2021, 57.6% of Richmond upon Thames residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 53.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 31.9% to 30.0%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Richmond upon Thames residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 2.9% to 2.6%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Richmond upon Thames decreased by 1.9 percentage points

Unpaid care in Richmond upon Thames

In 2021, 4.4% of Richmond upon Thames residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

This area had Greater London's joint third highest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (alongside Harrow). Across the region, only Bromley (4.6%) and Barnet (4.5%) had a higher proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Richmond upon Thames decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Richmond upon Thames

In 2021, 37.9% of Richmond upon Thames residents reported having "No religion", up from 28.4% in 2011. The rise of 9.5 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Richmond upon Thames. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across London, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 21.0% to 27.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 45.3% of people in Richmond upon Thames described themselves as Christian (down from 55.3%), while 7.1% did not state their religion (down from 8.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 37.9% of usual residents in Richmond upon Thames reported having "No religion"

National identity in Richmond upon Thames

Of Richmond upon Thames residents, 15.7% did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in 2021, up from 15.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 20 people (5.1%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 2.6% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Richmond upon Thames that identified as "British only" increased from 24.6% to 56.7%.

The percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was 22.5% (similar to 2011) across London. Across England, the percentage increased from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Richmond upon Thames increased by 0.7 percentage points
